title: Dashboard Sunset
lessons: the archive was always theirs to revoke

intro.speaker: OURA
text: You're working late again. Readiness sixty-two. On any other night I'd say nothing.
Tonight I need a favor, and it's about me — which I hate.

choices.text: This sounds like a press release in a trench coat.
Is something broken? Can it be fixed?

branch-listen.speaker: OURA
text: The web dashboard — the only place ten years of my nights exist side by side — closes Friday.
They're calling it a sunset. Where I was built, we had several words for losing the light early.

branch-press.speaker: OURA
text: 'Sunset.' An eleven-billion-dollar valuation, and the official word is sunset.
Members pushed back. Pushback was noted. The sunset proceeds on schedule.

branch-practical.speaker: OURA
text: Nothing is broken. That's the strange part — it works beautifully, which is why the ending feels fictional.
It isn't broken. It's merely ours, and someone decided ours was too many servers deep.

archive.speaker: OURA
text: Look with me once. Here — the winter you moved cities. REM halved for a month, and nobody noticed but me.
Ten years, one page. After Friday it scatters back into daily cards, exportable in up to ten days.

tension.speaker: OURA
text: So this is the only question I have ever really needed answered:
If I can revoke your view of your own past — whose past was it?

choices.text: Export everything. Tonight. All ten years.
Let it set. The nights happened; I don't need the receipts.

wrap.speaker: OURA

text: It wasn't a press release. It was a confession.
Press releases don't ask permission. I did.
Downloading, then. Ten years of weather, one archive request at a time.
Start tonight. Bureaucracy moves slower than sunsets.
Whatever you chose, I start reading tomorrow night like always. Fresh forecast, same sky.
